title: Intermittent output variance from adaptive kernel fusion due to selection-table hash collision shadowing prefetch slots
creator: Asha Patel
description: Observed nondeterministic numerical drift and token misordering for some prompts when adaptive kernel fusion is enabled. Root trigger appears to be hash collisions in the kernel selection remap table which cause prefetched KV slots to be shadowed by parallel fused kernel handoffs. This manifests as softmax output differences (low magnitude) that accumulate over multiple decoding steps and sometimes produce token skew for long-running generation. Impact seen on both A100 and H100 backends under high-concurrency workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: Enable adaptive kernel fusion (runtime flag: runtime.enable_adaptive_fusion = true)
Run batched prefill with fanout=8 and heterogenous sequence lengths (examples provided in reproducer gist)
Execute decode with continuous streaming for 200+ tokens per request, 4 concurrent requests
Observe occasional divergence vs baseline (fusion disabled) after ~30-120 tokens; seed-dependent and not deterministic every run
investigation_notes: Initial signal from customer (internal staging) reporting rare hallucination shifts in structured output; correlated with fusion rollout on dedicated clusters
Added deterministic run harness: reproducer/bench/kernel-fusion-repro.py (see links). Under debug build with guard rails, we captured 3 reproductions out of 250 runs.
Heap and KV allocator logs show two different kernel selection candidates mapping to the same remap index when a race between selector update and prefetch compaction occurs

Prefetch pipeline writes to KV slab indices before finalizing remap table; if remap entry is replaced (due to collision) concurrent decode may read the old slot while prefill continues, producing shadowed writes
Numerical differences appear as 1e-7 to 1e-4 per token softmax delta; amplified by layernorm and rotary interpolation over long sequences
Observed greater incidence under mixed-batch path optimizations (small/large sequence co-location) and when scheduler aggressively fuses kernels to avoid extra kernel launches
Stress tests show correlation with a specific hash seed used by the selection remap; switching to a 64-bit hash reduces frequency but does not eliminate bug
root_cause: Race between adaptive-kernel-selection remap table updates and prefetch writes: hash collisions lead to index reuse while prefetched KV entries are still being populated. The fusion path lacks sufficient write-ordering/visibility barriers for remap updates, allowing a decode path to read a partially populated or shadowed KV slot. This results in low-magnitude numerical drift that compounds across layers and tokens.
mitigations: Hotfix: Add write barrier on remap table update and sequence fence when compacting selection table (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1329). This serializes remap installs and eliminated reproductions in debug runs
Temporary rollback: disable adaptive kernel fusion on critical clusters via rollout flag runtime.fusion_rollout=off (console toggle applied to dedicated-pool-5)
Increase hash width to 64-bit for remap index to reduce collision frequency (mitigates but not full fix)
Add new unit tests and a determinism harness that runs fusion path under shuffled scheduling for 10k iterations
next_steps: Finalize barrier-based fix and bench for perf impact (benchmark target: <2% median latency regression for large-batch workloads)
Roll forward PR with staged canary: canary on non-prod clusters for 48h with continuous diff monitors (token-level KL divergence metric)
Add kernel-selection tombstone marker to detect stale reads in production; log rate-limited events to kernel-sentry (observability ticket pending)
Post-mortem writeup and integration into release notes, plus runbook for customers hitting similar symptoms
